name: workqueue-package
description: The package as a deployment uses it: its behaviors register with an engine through the plug-in interface, carry the declarations the core binary writes, and run the document the core binary builds in the CLI smoke (fixture-workqueue-json), whose jobs compose Workflow, Lease, Assignment, Queue, Budget and Retries: workers claim them in order, each claim reserving its budget, hold and renew their leases and record their attempts, and the runner puts a job whose time ran out back in the queue, settling what it reserved. The fixture's other files hold one type each, which run as schemas of their own: a worker with Presence, which releases its principal's leases on jobs, and a batch whose Blueprint stamps steps.

shared.s1: An exclusive, time-bounded lease on the instance, held by one principal and numbered by a fencing token that advances at every acquire, release and expiry. While the lease is active only its holder may change the instance, and a write that presents a token other than the current one, as Lease's precondition, is refused whoever calls; a heartbeat with the current token renews the lease and delivers the directives sent to the holder. A lease its holder stops renewing expires, and the expiry can move the instance's Workflow status back.

shared.s5: Ends an active lease: the holder, presenting the current token as Lease's precondition, or a principal with overridePermission, who need not. The token advances, so the directives sent under the lease are not delivered again, and onExpiry moves the status when it is still one of its from states. With abandon, the holder gives the work up as failed: the release counts as an expiry, and escalate applies at the one that reaches maxExpiries.
shared.s6: Applies the expiry of a lease past its expiry time or its longest hold: the holder is cleared, the token advances, the expiry is counted unless the instance is in a terminal state of its Workflow, and onExpiry or escalate moves the status. Any principal who may write the instance may call it; on any other instance it changes nothing. With holder, a principal with overridePermission expires that holder's lease at once, active or not, unless notRenewedAfter spares it. The engine's runner calls it on every lapsed lease, every sweepMs.

holder.description: The principal whose lease to expire now, active or not; it needs overridePermission.

notRenewedAfter.description: With holder: an active lease its holder acquired or renewed after this time, in epoch milliseconds, is spared, since its own heartbeats show the process holding it is alive. A lapsed one expires all the same.

shared.s8: Sends the holder of the active lease a directive, which its heartbeats deliver until it acknowledges it. With dedupeKey, a directive already sent under the lease with the key is not sent again. A principal needs directPermission, or overridePermission when that is absent, and is refused when the config names neither; another behavior of the type sends one with call(), as the principal it runs for, without either.

dedupeKey.description: Sends the directive once per lease: when one was sent under the current token with this key, acknowledged or not, that one stands and nothing is sent.

ids.description: The instances whose lease expired, by id.

shared.s13: Makes the type's instances claimable work. claim checks that an instance can be claimed, takes its lease and moves its Workflow status from a claimable state to the claimed one, in one transaction; claimNext claims the first instance that can be claimed, highest priority first, then oldest, and countClaimable counts them. Candidates come from copies of what a claim checks, kept current as the instance and what it waits on change, so work that cannot be claimed now (blocked, over budget, exhausted, pinned to a superseded revision) is not tried. Requires Workflow and Lease.

shared.s19: Reserve-then-settle budgets on the instance, in units the deployment names. Each meter counts what the instance has used and the reservations it holds against its limit. A reservation that does not fit here, or in an enclosing scope that a Links link points at, is refused, and the whole chain is left as it was. Usage is never refused: it draws the instance's own reservation down, counts here and in every enclosing scope, reports each instance it takes over its limit, and can move the status of each through escalate. checkReserve answers whether a reservation would fit now, which Queue copies so that work over its budget is not tried. On a type that composes Lease, a reservation lives as long as the lease it was made under.

The meter's remaining, which the reservation fits while it is at or above the number; where a daily meter keeps it out now, the scope's reserved and limit; and the link to the scope's own scope.

until.description: When it does not fit: the start of the next UTC day, when the daily meters starting again make it fit with nothing else changing; null when only a change can make it fit, and when it fits.

shared.s28: Retries per failure class. Each attempt is recorded with recordAttempt: a success, or a failure of a class the config names, which counts against that class's cap and a total cap. A terminal class, a failure past a cap, or the same failure signature repeated stuckAfter times exhausts the instance, and its Workflow status moves to exhaustedState from the config's from states through Workflow's transition. Once exhausted, its status moves only to exhaustedState and its lease cannot be taken. A kept result, the best scoring one when keepBest is given, is written to resultField with the checks of an update. There is no backoff in time. Requires Workflow.

acquirePermission.description: The permission a principal needs to acquire a lease. Absent, any principal who may write the instance can.

directOn.description: Directives the engine's runner sends the holder of an instance's active lease when the target of one of the instance's links moves on: a new revision of Revisions, or a release of Branches; for a pinned link, a revision tells only the instances the target moved past. The runner sends each with direct, as its principal, which needs directPermission, or overridePermission when that is absent, once per lease and move (dedupeKey). An instance with no lease held hears nothing, and its next holder nothing either. Needs Links on the type; one entry per link.

data.description: Its data, beside revised, which the runner sets: the link, the target's schema and id, and its revision or the release's commit.

name.description: The directive's name, as direct takes it.

revised.description: The link whose target's move sends the directive.

link.description: A link of the type's Links config.

directPermission.description: The permission a principal needs to send the holder a directive; overridePermission when absent. With neither, direct is refused.

escalate.description: Used instead of onExpiry at the expiry or abandon that reaches maxExpiries, which it needs. Needs Workflow on the type.

from.description: The states the status moves from; in any other state it stays.

transition.description: The state to move to, through Workflow's transition.

exempt.description: Writing operations of the type's other behaviors, each as <Behavior>.<operation>, that a principal other than the holder may run while the lease is active, and that requireToken does not hold to the token.

heartbeatMs.description: How often the holder should send a heartbeat, in milliseconds, at most half of ttlMs, so one late heartbeat does not lose the lease; a third of ttlMs when absent. acquire returns it.

maxExpiries.description: How many expiries an instance may have, abandons included. Once it has had this many, its lease cannot be acquired again until resetExpiries.

maxHoldField.description: An integer field of the type that gives the instance's own longest hold, in milliseconds. When the instance holds a positive integer there, it overrides maxHoldMs.

maxHoldMs.description: The longest a principal may hold a lease after acquiring it, in milliseconds, renewed or not; no limit when absent.

onExpiry.description: Moves the instance's Workflow status when a lease ends with the work unfinished: at an expiry, an abandon and a release, while the status is one of from. Needs Workflow on the type.

from.description: The states the status moves from; in any other state it stays.

transition.description: The state to move to, through Workflow's transition.

overridePermission.description: The permission that lets a principal release another principal's lease, change the instance while another principal holds its lease, reset its expiries, and send directives when directPermission is absent.

requireToken.description: When true, a write to an instance with an active lease that does not present the current token as Lease's precondition is refused, the holder's own included, so every process of a principal fences its writes. Exempt and read-only operations, Lease's own operations and a principal with overridePermission are not held to it.

sweepMs.description: How often the engine's runner expires the leases past their expiry time or longest hold, in milliseconds; 5000 when absent.

ttlMs.description: How long a lease lasts after its acquire or its last heartbeat, in milliseconds; 60000 when absent.

operations.name: acquire
operations.description: Takes the lease for the caller and returns its fencing token. Refused while a lease is active, the caller's own included (heartbeat renews it), without acquirePermission when the config names one, and once the instance has had maxExpiries expiries. Over a lease that expired, it applies that expiry first.

ttlMs.description: How long the lease lasts after its acquire and each heartbeat, in milliseconds, at most the config's ttlMs; the config's when absent.

operations.name: heartbeat
operations.description: Renews the lease, never past its longest hold, acknowledges the directives acknowledge names, and returns the directives sent under it that are not acknowledged. Only the holder, presenting the current token as Lease's precondition, while the lease is active: an expired lease cannot be renewed.

acknowledge.description: Directives of the lease to mark handled first, as acknowledge does, so a heartbeat acknowledges in the same write; empty, none.

abandon.description: Whether the work is given up as failed, so the release counts as an expiry.

reason.description: Why, when one expired: ttl, its holder stopped renewing it; maxHold, it reached its longest hold; holder, it was active and expired by its holder's name.

created.description: Whether this call sent it; false when one with dedupeKey was already sent.

id.description: The directive's number in its lease: the one sent, or the one already sent with dedupeKey.

operations.name: acknowledge
operations.description: Marks directives of the lease as handled, so heartbeats stop delivering them. Only the holder, presenting the current token as Lease's precondition.

operations.name: expireHolder
operations.description: Expires every lease one principal holds on the schema's instances, active or not, as expire with that holder does on each: for a principal that is gone. With notRenewedAfter, an active lease renewed after that time is spared. Needs overridePermission; refused when the config names none.

holder.description: The principal whose leases to expire.

notRenewedAfter.description: As expire's: an active lease acquired or renewed after this time is spared.

operations.name: resetExpiries
operations.description: Sets the instance's count of expiries back to 0, so a lease can be acquired again after maxExpiries. Needs overridePermission; refused when the config names none.

token.description: The lease's current fencing token, as acquire returned it: a write that presents another is refused (token_stale).

expect.name: Assignment
expect.description: Assigns the instance to one principal at a time. A principal may assign an unassigned instance to itself and unassign itself; assigning another principal, reassigning, and unassigning another principal need the config's permission. While the instance is assigned, only its assignee may take its lease (Lease's acquire) or claim it (Queue's claim).

permission.description: The permission a principal needs to assign the instance to another principal, reassign it, or unassign another principal. Absent, only the first two self-service moves are possible.

fields.name: assignee
fields.description: The principal the instance is assigned to; absent when it is unassigned.

operations.name: assign
operations.description: Assigns the instance to a principal: the caller itself when it is unassigned, or anyone, reassigning included, with the config's permission.

operations.name: unassign
operations.description: Clears the assignment: the assignee itself, or a principal with the config's permission.

assignee.description: The principal it was assigned to.

claim.description: The Workflow states an instance is claimed from, and the state a claim moves it to.

from.description: The states an instance can be claimed in; a transition from each to the claimed state must exist.

to.description: The state a claim moves the instance to.

excludeStale.description: Pinned links of the type's Links config: an instance one of which is pinned to a revision or a release its target has moved past is not claimed, and is no candidate until a change of it, a new link say, lets it back in.

match.description: The type's own top-level scalar fields claimNext and countClaimable may filter on, by equality with a value or membership in a list of values.

maxCandidates.description: The most instances one claimNext tries before it gives up; 100 when absent.

priorityField.description: An integer field of the type that orders claimNext: higher first, an instance without a value last. Absent, oldest first.

operations.name: claim
operations.description: Claims the instance for the caller: its status must be one of the claimable states, no blocker may hold it up, and no link excludeStale names may be stale; then it takes the lease and moves the status to the claimed state, or does neither.

ttlMs.description: The lease's length, as Lease's acquire takes it.

operations.name: claimNext
operations.description: Claims the first instance of the schema the caller can claim, highest priority first, then oldest, skipping each one whose claim is refused (vetoed, conflict or forbidden), up to maxCandidates; null when none can be claimed. An instance its copies show blocked, at maxExpiries, assigned to another principal, over its budget, exhausted or pinned to a superseded revision is no candidate.

operations.name: countClaimable
operations.description: Counts the instances of the schema claimNext would try for the caller, with the same eligibility and no maxCandidates: a signal of the work waiting, which reads and changes nothing else.

count.description: How many instances are candidates now.

expect.name: Presence
expect.description: A heartbeat on an instance that stands for a worker: the principal whose subject the instance's principalField holds beats it, and an instance not beaten within ttlMs of its create or its last beat is missed. A miss can move the instance's Workflow status and expire the leases the principal holds on the schemas the config names, but for the ones renewed since its last beat; the engine's runner applies the misses every sweepMs.

onBeat.description: Moves the instance's Workflow status at a beat, while the status is one of from: the way back from the state onMissed moves it to. Needs Workflow on the type.

from.description: The states the status moves from; in any other state it stays.

transition.description: The state to move to, through Workflow's transition.

onMissed.description: Moves the instance's Workflow status when it is missed, while the status is one of from. Needs Workflow on the type.

from.description: The states the status moves from; in any other state it stays.

transition.description: The state to move to, through Workflow's transition.

principalField.description: A string field of the type that holds the subject of the principal the instance stands for, the only principal that may beat it. Once set, it cannot change.

releaseLeases.description: Schemas that compose Lease, whose leases the principal holds are expired when the instance is missed, through Lease's schema-level expireHolder, but for a lease renewed after the principal's last beat, whose own heartbeats show it alive. The principal that applies the miss, the runner's in the sweep, needs Lease's overridePermission on each.

sweepMs.description: How often the engine's runner misses the instances past their deadline, in milliseconds; 5000 when absent.

ttlMs.description: How long the instance stays present after its create or its last beat, in milliseconds.

fields.name: deadline
fields.description: When the instance is missed unless it is beaten, in epoch milliseconds: ttlMs after its create or its last beat; absent on an instance made before the schema composed Presence, until its first beat.

fields.name: lastBeatAt
fields.description: When the instance was last beaten, in epoch milliseconds; absent before the first beat.

fields.name: missed
fields.description: Whether the instance missed its deadline and has not been beaten since.

fields.name: released
fields.description: The instances whose lease the last miss expired, by schema; absent before a miss.

operations.name: beat
operations.description: Moves the deadline to ttlMs from now and clears missed, and onBeat moves the status when it is one of its from states. Only the principal whose subject the instance's principalField holds.

deadline.description: When the instance is missed unless beaten again, in epoch milliseconds.

operations.name: miss
operations.description: Applies the miss of an instance past its deadline and not missed yet: sets missed, moves the status with onMissed when it is one of its from states, and expires the principal's leases on the releaseLeases schemas that were not renewed after its last beat, recording which in released. Any principal who may write the instance may call it; on any other instance it changes nothing. The engine's runner calls it every sweepMs.

missed.description: Whether this call missed the instance.

released.description: When it did: the instances whose lease it expired, by releaseLeases schema; empty when another instance that stands for the principal is present.

vetoes.description: The instance's principalField holds no principal, so no one may beat it.
The instance stands for another principal, who alone may beat it.
principalField holds the principal the instance stands for, and does not change once set.

expect.name: Blueprint
expect.description: Creates the instance's children from a map of steps: one instance of the child schema per step, created with its link to the instance and blocked by the children of the steps it comes after, all in one transaction that a failure refuses whole. The steps are inline in the config, stamped when the instance is created, or held by a definition the instance links to, pinned to a revision, stamped when that link is first set, by the create that gives it or a later link. A step can depend on the instance's fields (when); a step left out passes its dependencies on to the steps that come after it.

copyFields.description: Fields of this type copied to every child, a field of the child's type of the same name.

copyLinks.description: Links of this type copied to every child, a link of the child's Links config of the same name to the same schema, keeping the revision or the release this instance's link records where the child's pins the same: the links the instance holds when it is stamped, which for inline steps are the ones its create gives.

from.description: Where the steps are kept as an instance: a link of this type's Links config pinned to a revision, and the field of the linked instance that holds a map of steps of the same form as steps. The steps are read from the revision the link pins and stamped when the link is first set, by the create that gives it or a later link.

field.description: The field of the linked instance's type that holds the steps.

link.description: A link of this type's Links config pinned to a revision.

keyField.description: A string field of the child schema's type that each child gets its step's key in.

parentLink.description: The link of the child schema's Links config that points at this schema; each child is linked to its parent through it.

schema.description: The child schema. It composes Links with parentLink, Constants over keyField and every copied field, Dependencies when a step comes after another, and not Blueprint.

after.description: The keys of the steps whose children block this step's child.

data.description: Fields of the child, beside its key and the copied fields.

when.description: Stamps the step only when the instance's field equals a value, or is a list that includes one; absent, always.

equals.description: The value the field must equal, as JSON.

field.description: A field of this schema's type.

includes.description: A value the field, a list, must include, as JSON.

steps.description: The steps, by key, stamped when the instance is created.

fields.name: children
fields.description: What was stamped: each step's key and its child's id, in the order they were created; absent until the instance is stamped.

vetoes.description: Links' link moving the from link once the instance's children were stamped from the revision it pins.
A stamp whose steps come after others, while the child schema does not compose Dependencies.
A stamp while the child schema's Constants does not keep keyField and every copied field, which a later version of it dropped; details.fields lists the ones it does not keep.
A stamp from a from link that records no revision to read the steps from.
A stamp from a pinned revision of the definition the principal cannot read.
A stamp from a map of steps that is not valid for this type.

escalate.description: Moves the instance's Workflow status when usage leaves it over the limit of a meter, while the status is one of from, in the transaction of that usage: an instance's own usage, or one an instance inside it passes up, so a scope's config moves the scope. A move a guard vetoes or the caller may not make leaves the status, and the usage counts all the same. Needs Workflow on the type.

from.description: The states the status moves from; in any other state it stays.

transition.description: The state to move to, through Workflow's transition.

limitPermission.description: The permission a principal needs to change a meter's limit, with setLimit or through limitField. Absent, no limit changes once the instance exists.

limit.description: The most the instance may have used and reserved together; with limitField, the limit while the field holds no value of at least 0. No limit of its own when neither gives one.

limitField.description: An integer field of the type that holds the instance's limit; while it holds no value of at least 0, limit is the limit, and without limit there is none. Only a principal with limitPermission changes it once the instance exists.

reserve.description: The amount reserve takes for the meter when it is given no meter: what a claim reserves. With reserveField, the amount when the field holds no positive integer.

reserveField.description: An integer field of the type whose positive value is the amount reserve takes for the meter when it is given no meter, in place of reserve.

reset.description: daily: the used amount starts again at 0 at each UTC day; reservations are kept.

scope.description: A link of the type's Links config whose target is the enclosing scope: its schema composes Budget with the same meter, and every reservation and usage of the meter here is taken there too, and on up its own scope.

meters.description: The meters, by name: camelCase, at most 64 characters.

onExceeded.description: A directive sent to the holder of the instance's active lease, through Lease's direct, when usage takes the instance or an enclosing scope over its limit: once per meter per lease. Needs Lease on the type.

direct.description: The directive's name. Its data is { meter, used, limit, scope }, scope being the instance over its limit as { schema, id }.

fields.name: meters
fields.description: Each meter, by name: used, reserved (this instance's own reservation and what it holds for the instances inside it), limit and remaining (limit minus used and reserved), limit and remaining null when the meter has no limit. A daily meter whose day has passed shows used 0.

operations.name: reserve
operations.description: Reserves an amount of one meter, or of every meter the config gives a reservation, for the instance and every enclosing scope. Refused when the instance or an enclosing scope cannot fit it, and then nothing is reserved anywhere. On a type that composes Lease it needs an active lease, and the reservation is settled when that lease ends.

amount.description: How much to reserve of the meter; its configured reservation when absent. Needs meter.

meter.description: The meter; every meter with a configured reservation when absent.

reserved.description: What this call reserved, by meter.

operations.name: checkReserve
operations.description: Whether reserve with the same parameters would fit now, here and in every enclosing scope, after the reservations of a lease that is no longer active are settled, as reserve settles them; it changes nothing and does not ask for a lease. Queue copies its answer so that a claim that cannot fit is not tried.

amount.description: How much of the meter; its configured reservation when absent. Needs meter.

meter.description: The meter; every meter with a configured reservation when absent.

operations.name: settle
operations.description: Releases the instance's own reservation of one meter, or of every meter, here and in every enclosing scope.

meter.description: The meter; every meter when absent.

released.description: What this call released, by meter.

operations.name: setLimit
operations.description: Sets a meter's limit on the instance, raising or lowering it; through limitField when the meter has one. Needs limitPermission, and is refused when the config names none, and below what the instance has used and reserved.

previous.description: The limit before; null when there was none.

operations.name: reserveFor
operations.description: Holds an amount of a meter for an instance whose scope link points here, as that instance's reserve does, and passes it on up this instance's own scope. Refused when the amount does not fit, when that instance does not draw the meter from here, and beyond what it has reserved and this instance does not hold for it yet.

held.description: What this instance now holds of the meter for that one.

operations.name: settleFor
operations.description: Releases up to an amount of what this instance holds of a meter for another, never more than that one no longer holds itself, and passes the release on up this instance's own scope.

operations.name: recordUsageFor
operations.description: Counts usage of a meter by an instance whose scope link points here, releases the part of what this instance holds for it that its own reservation covered, never more than that one no longer holds, and passes both on up this instance's own scope. Never refused for the amount.

attempts.description: How many failures of the class an instance may have.

hint.description: What recordAttempt returns for a failure of the class, to steer the worker's next attempt.

classes.description: The failure classes, by name: each its own cap of attempts, with an optional hint for the next attempt, or terminal, which exhausts the instance at its first failure.

exhaustedState.description: The state of the type's Workflow an exhausted instance moves to.

from.description: The states exhaustion moves the status from; every state but the terminal ones and exhaustedState when absent. A transition from each to exhaustedState must exist.

keepBest.description: Keeps the best scoring result rather than only a success's: a failed attempt's result is kept when its score beats the best kept one by at least minDelta and no neverRegress predicate that held for the kept one fails.

minDelta.description: How much a score must beat the best kept one by; any amount above it when absent.

neverRegress.description: Predicates an attempt reports that a kept result never loses: one true for the kept result must be true for the next one kept.

limitsField.description: An object field of the type with the instance's own caps: a class's name to a cap of at least 0, and totalAttempts to a total of at least 1. An unknown or terminal class, and a value that is not such an integer, is ignored. Once the instance exists, only a principal with limitsPermission changes it, and the holder of its active lease does not.

limitsPermission.description: The permission a principal needs to change limitsField once the instance exists. Absent, the caps an instance is created with do not change.

permission.description: The permission a principal needs to record an attempt. Absent, any principal who may write the instance can.

resultField.description: A field of the type a kept result is written to, with the checks of an update.

stuckAfter.description: How many failures in a row, none of them kept, with the same signature exhaust the instance as stuck.

totalAttempts.description: How many failures of every class together an instance may have.

scenarios.name: the work-queue package (node) > it runs the document the core binary builds: claimed in order, held, and put back when its time runs out

expect.name: jobs
expect.description: A job an engine runs with the core's work-queue behaviors and no extension: a worker claims the queued job of a topic with the highest priority, holds its lease while it runs, and a lease that expires puts the job back in the queue, until its third expiry fails it. A claim reserves CPU seconds from a daily budget, and a failed attempt is retried per failure class until its caps fail the job.

priority.description: Signed 64-bit integer; range bounded by JavaScript's safe-integer ceiling.

timeLimitMs.description: Signed 64-bit integer; range bounded by JavaScript's safe-integer ceiling.

instanceBehaviors.description: The instance's behaviors' fields, by behavior name, apart from its own fields

status.description: The state the instance is in.

enteredAt.description: When the status last changed, in epoch milliseconds: the create's time, then each transition's. Absent on an instance created before Workflow kept it, until its next transition.

holder.description: The subject of the principal that holds the lease; absent when the instance is free.

token.description: The fencing token. It advances at every acquire, release and expiry, and a write under the lease presents it.

acquiredAt.description: When the lease was acquired, in epoch milliseconds; absent when the instance is free.

renewedAt.description: Its acquire or its last heartbeat, in epoch milliseconds; absent when the instance is free.

expiresAt.description: When the lease expires unless it is renewed, in epoch milliseconds; absent when the instance is free.

active.description: Whether a lease is held and has not expired.

expiries.description: How many leases have expired or been abandoned since the last resetExpiries.

ended.description: How and when the last lease ended (reason and at); absent while one is held.

assignee.description: The principal the instance is assigned to; absent when it is unassigned.

meters.description: Each meter, by name: used, reserved (this instance's own reservation and what it holds for the instances inside it), limit and remaining (limit minus used and reserved), limit and remaining null when the meter has no limit. A daily meter whose day has passed shows used 0.

bestScore.description: The score of the kept result; absent when no scored result is kept.

exhausted.description: Whether the instance has run out of attempts.

stuck.description: Whether the instance failed with the same signature stuckAfter times in a row.

behaviors.name: Workflow
behaviors.description: A state machine on the instance: a status that starts in the initial state and changes only through transition, along a transition the config lists. A transition may name a permission the caller must hold. A state that no transition leaves is terminal, and a terminal state has an outcome: success, failure or neutral, success unless the config says otherwise. Other instances' blockers, rollups and reactions read it.
behaviors.summary: Its status is one of queued, running, done and failed; a new Job starts in queued, and status moves only by transition. Terminal, with their outcomes: done (success) and failed (success).

fields.name: status
fields.description: The state the instance is in.

fields.name: enteredAt
fields.description: When the status last changed, in epoch milliseconds: the create's time, then each transition's. Absent on an instance created before Workflow kept it, until its next transition.

vetoes.description: The instance is already in the state the transition names.
The instance is in a terminal state: no transition leaves it.
No transition of the config leads from the instance's state to the one named.
The instance has no status to move from.

behaviors.name: Lease
behaviors.summary: A lease gives one principal the Job for 30 seconds at a time, renewed by heartbeat at least every 10 seconds, and held at most the instance's timeLimitMs milliseconds. The runner expires a lapsed lease within 5 seconds; an expiry moves status from running to queued. After 3 expiries it is not leased again, and that expiry moves status from running to failed instead. While a lease is active only its holder writes; each acquire gives a new token, which the holder presents as preconditions {"Lease": {"token": n}}.

behaviors.name: Assignment
behaviors.description: Assigns the instance to one principal at a time. A principal may assign an unassigned instance to itself and unassign itself; assigning another principal, reassigning, and unassigning another principal need the config's permission. While the instance is assigned, only its assignee may take its lease (Lease's acquire) or claim it (Queue's claim).
behaviors.summary: Each Job is assigned to one principal or none; while it is assigned, only its assignee acquires its lease or claims it. A principal assigns an unassigned instance to itself and unassigns itself; assigning another principal, reassigning and unassigning another need permission jobs.assign.

fields.name: assignee
fields.description: The principal the instance is assigned to; absent when it is unassigned.

behaviors.name: Queue
behaviors.summary: A claim takes an instance in queued: its lease, its budget reservation, and a move to running, in one write. claimNext claims the first the caller can, highest priority first, then oldest first, matching topic, trying at most 100. An instance is not claimed while it is exhausted (Retries), over its budget, here or in an enclosing scope (Budget), at 3 lease expiries or assigned to another principal.

behaviors.name: Budget
behaviors.summary: Meters: cpuSeconds (limit 3600; reserving 600 at a claim; counted per UTC day). A reservation fits while used plus reserved plus the amount is within the limit, here and in each enclosing scope; it is made under the active lease and settled when the lease ends.

fields.name: meters
fields.description: Each meter, by name: used, reserved (this instance's own reservation and what it holds for the instances inside it), limit and remaining (limit minus used and reserved), limit and remaining null when the meter has no limit. A daily meter whose day has passed shows used 0.

behaviors.name: Retries
behaviors.summary: Failure classes: invalidOutput (2 attempts), rejected (terminal: one failure exhausts) and timeout (3 attempts); at most 4 counted failures in all. Once exhausted, status moves from queued or running to failed, and the Job takes no more attempts, moves only to failed, and is not acquired or claimed.

operations.name: create
operations.title: Create jobs
operations.description: Creates a jobs: validates the instance, data, against the schema's live version and stores it under id, or under a new id when none is given.

id.description: The instance id; the engine makes one when it is absent

guidance.useWhen: Use to create a new Job: data holds its own fields, and id names it, or the engine makes one.
guidance.doNotUseWhen: Do not use to change one that exists; call update.
guidance.success: Returns the new instance with its id, its seq, its own fields in data and its behaviors' fields in behaviors, by behavior name. A new instance's status is queued.

operations.name: get
operations.title: Get jobs
operations.description: Returns the jobs with the id: its own fields in data, its behaviors' in behaviors.

valueRefs.description: Return each field the value store holds as its ref, { "$value": <hash>, "bytes": <n> }, listed in valueRefs, rather than its value, which get_value reads

guidance.useWhen: Use when you have the id of the Job to read.
guidance.doNotUseWhen: Do not use to find Job instances; call list.
guidance.success: Returns the instance with its seq, its own fields in data and its behaviors' fields in behaviors, by behavior name.

operations.name: list
operations.title: List jobs
operations.description: Lists jobs instances in creation order, a page at a time: pass a page's next as cursor for the page after it. where keeps the instances whose fields hold the values it gives, a list meaning any of them; a filtered page can hold fewer than limit while next is not null.

limit.description: How many instances a page holds, 50 when absent

valueRefs.description: Return each field the value store holds as its ref, { "$value": <hash>, "bytes": <n> }, listed in valueRefs, rather than its value, which get_value reads

where.description: The values the instances hold, by field: a value, null for none, or a list of 1 to 100 meaning any of them; every member must hold

anyOf.description: The state the instance is in.

items.description: The state the instance is in.

anyOf.description: The principal that holds its lease, a lapsed one included until its expiry is applied; null for a free instance.

items.description: The principal that holds its lease, a lapsed one included until its expiry is applied; null for a free instance.

anyOf.description: The principal the instance is assigned to; absent when it is unassigned.

items.description: The principal the instance is assigned to; absent when it is unassigned.

next.description: The next page's cursor; null after the last page

guidance.useWhen: Use to page through Job instances, oldest first. where keeps the ones whose fields hold the values it gives, null meaning no value and a list of values any of them: title, topic, priority, timeLimitMs, Workflow.status, Lease.holder, Assignment.assignee or Retries.exhausted; a behavior's field by its qualified name, the behavior's, a dot and the field's. where: { "Workflow.status": <state> } lists the instances in one of queued, running, done or failed, and a list of states the instances in any of them. where: { "Lease.holder": <subject> } lists the Job instances whose lease a principal holds, a lapsed one until the runner expires it, and "Lease.holder": null the free ones. where: { "Assignment.assignee": <subject> } lists the Job instances assigned to a principal, "Assignment.assignee": null the unassigned ones, and [null, <subject>] both. where: { "Retries.exhausted": true } lists the Job instances whose retries are exhausted, and false the ones that may run again.
guidance.doNotUseWhen: Do not use to read one instance whose id you have; call get.
guidance.success: Returns items and next; pass next as cursor for the page after, until it is null. With where, a page can hold fewer items than limit, even none, while next is not null: read on until it is.

operations.name: update
operations.title: Update jobs
operations.description: Applies a JSON merge patch (RFC 7386) to the jobs with the id: a member replaces the instance's, a nested object merges and null removes a member. With expectedSeq the update is refused unless the instance is still at that sequence.

expectedSeq.description: The sequence the caller last read (an instance's seq): the call is refused unless the instance is still at it

patch.description: A JSON merge patch of the Job

guidance.useWhen: Use to change the own fields of the Job with the id, as a JSON merge patch; with expectedSeq, the update is refused if the instance changed since that seq.
guidance.doNotUseWhen: Do not use to set a behavior's field: the patch holds own fields only, and a behavior's fields change only through its operations. Do not use to move Workflow's status, which behaviors.Workflow holds; call transition. Do not write under another principal's active lease; the holder may present its token as preconditions {"Lease": {"token": n}}, which a newer lease makes stale. timeLimitMs does not change while a lease is held.
guidance.success: Returns the instance as the patch left it, with its next seq.

errors.description: Lease: Another principal holds the instance's active lease.
errors.commonCorrection: Wait until expiresAt in details, or work on another instance.

errors.description: Lease: The token the call presents as Lease's precondition is not the lease's current one: a newer lease, or none, has replaced the one it names.
errors.commonCorrection: Stop: a newer lease replaced yours. Read behaviors.Lease, and acquire again only if it is free.

errors.description: Lease: The lease is past its expiry time or its longest hold: it gives its holder nothing, and only its expiry can follow.
errors.commonCorrection: Stop working on the instance: the lease has lapsed. Acquire it again once it has expired.

errors.description: Lease: maxHoldField cannot change while a lease is held.
errors.commonCorrection: Change the field once the lease has ended, or with the override permission.

operations.name: delete
operations.title: Delete jobs
operations.description: Deletes the jobs with the id. With expectedSeq the delete is refused unless the instance is still at that sequence.

expectedSeq.description: The sequence the caller last read (an instance's seq): the call is refused unless the instance is still at it

guidance.useWhen: Use to delete the Job with the id for good; with expectedSeq, the delete is refused if the instance changed since that seq.
guidance.doNotUseWhen: Do not write under another principal's active lease; the holder may present its token as preconditions {"Lease": {"token": n}}, which a newer lease makes stale.
guidance.success: Returns null; the instance and what its behaviors kept for it are gone.

operations.name: transition
operations.title: jobs: transition
operations.description: Moves the instance to another state along a transition the config lists. A transition that names a permission needs a caller who holds it.

expectedSeq.description: The sequence the caller last read (an instance's seq): the call is refused unless the instance is still at it

from.description: The state the instance was in.

to.description: The state it is in now.

guidance.useWhen: Use to move status from queued to running or failed; from running to queued, done or failed.
guidance.doNotUseWhen: Do not use from done or failed: no transition leaves a terminal state. Do not use to stay where the instance is. Do not write under another principal's active lease; the holder may present its token as preconditions {"Lease": {"token": n}}, which a newer lease makes stale. Do not move an exhausted instance anywhere but failed.
guidance.success: Returns from and to; status holds to from then on, and enteredAt the time of the move.

errors.description: Workflow: No transition leads from the instance's status to the state named; details.allowed lists the states it can move to.
errors.commonCorrection: Read status, then name a state details.allowed lists, or move through one of them first.

errors.description: Workflow: The instance is already in the state the transition names.
errors.commonCorrection: Read status: the instance is already there, so nothing needs to move.

errors.description: Workflow: The instance is in a terminal state: no transition leaves it.
errors.commonCorrection: None: the work has ended. Create a new instance to start again.

errors.description: Workflow: The instance has no status to move from.
errors.commonCorrection: None: an instance without a status cannot move.

errors.description: Lease: Another principal holds the instance's active lease.
errors.commonCorrection: Wait until expiresAt in details, or work on another instance.

errors.description: Lease: The token the call presents as Lease's precondition is not the lease's current one: a newer lease, or none, has replaced the one it names.
errors.commonCorrection: Stop: a newer lease replaced yours. Read behaviors.Lease, and acquire again only if it is free.

errors.description: Lease: The lease is past its expiry time or its longest hold: it gives its holder nothing, and only its expiry can follow.
errors.commonCorrection: Stop working on the instance: the lease has lapsed. Acquire it again once it has expired.

errors.description: Retries: The instance's retries are exhausted: it takes no more attempts, its status moves only to exhaustedState, and it is not acquired or claimed again.
errors.commonCorrection: None: the instance takes no more attempts; create new work instead.

operations.name: acquire
operations.title: jobs: acquire
operations.description: Takes the lease for the caller and returns its fencing token. Refused while a lease is active, the caller's own included (heartbeat renews it), without acquirePermission when the config names one, and once the instance has had maxExpiries expiries. Over a lease that expired, it applies that expiry first.

expectedSeq.description: The sequence the caller last read (an instance's seq): the call is refused unless the instance is still at it

ttlMs.description: How long the lease lasts after its acquire and each heartbeat, in milliseconds, at most the config's ttlMs; the config's when absent.

guidance.useWhen: Use to take the lease, for 30 seconds or a shorter ttlMs, before working on the instance alone.
guidance.doNotUseWhen: Do not use on an instance assigned to another principal. Do not use: on Job the lease is taken by claim or claimNext. Do not use once behaviors.Retries.exhausted is true.
guidance.success: Returns token, expiresAt and heartbeatMs: heartbeat at least every heartbeatMs and present the token as preconditions {"Lease": {"token": n}} on each write.

errors.description: Lease: Another principal holds the instance's active lease.
errors.commonCorrection: Wait until expiresAt in details, or work on another instance.

errors.description: Lease: The caller already holds the active lease: acquire refuses it, and heartbeat renews it.
errors.commonCorrection: Keep the lease you hold: renew it with heartbeat.

errors.description: Lease: The token the call presents as Lease's precondition is not the lease's current one: a newer lease, or none, has replaced the one it names.
errors.commonCorrection: Stop: a newer lease replaced yours. Read behaviors.Lease, and acquire again only if it is free.

errors.description: Lease: The instance has had maxExpiries expiries, so its lease cannot be acquired until resetExpiries.
errors.commonCorrection: A caller with the override permission resets the count with resetExpiries.

errors.description: Assignment: The instance is assigned to another principal, who alone may acquire its lease or claim it.
errors.commonCorrection: Take work assigned to you or to no one, or have it unassigned first.

errors.description: Queue: The lease of a claimable instance is taken by claiming it, not by Lease's acquire.
errors.commonCorrection: Call claim, or claimNext.

errors.description: Retries: The instance's retries are exhausted: it takes no more attempts, its status moves only to exhaustedState, and it is not acquired or claimed again.
errors.commonCorrection: None: the instance takes no more attempts; create new work instead.

operations.name: heartbeat
operations.title: jobs: heartbeat
operations.description: Renews the lease, never past its longest hold, acknowledges the directives acknowledge names, and returns the directives sent under it that are not acknowledged. Only the holder, presenting the current token as Lease's precondition, while the lease is active: an expired lease cannot be renewed.

expectedSeq.description: The sequence the caller last read (an instance's seq): the call is refused unless the instance is still at it

acknowledge.description: Directives of the lease to mark handled first, as acknowledge does, so a heartbeat acknowledges in the same write; empty, none.

guidance.useWhen: Use as the holder at least every 10 seconds, presenting the token, to keep the lease; acknowledge takes the ids of directives handled.
guidance.success: Returns the new expiresAt and the directives not yet acknowledged, oldest first.

expectedSeq.description: The sequence the caller last read (an instance's seq): the call is refused unless the instance is still at it

abandon.description: Whether the work is given up as failed, so the release counts as an expiry.
